summary: This bill requires the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to issue rules within 180 days allowing transmission providers to propose—and get approved within 60 days—adjustments that move dispatchable power projects ahead in interconnection queues, after showing need, improving reliability or resilience, and allowing public comment.

scores.thoughts: The bill directs FERC to conduct rulemaking on interconnection procedures but contains no provisions authorizing, expanding, or reducing any federal expenditures or appropriations. It is purely regulatory in nature.
No provisions in the bill address tax rates, credits, deductions, or any tax policy matters.
The bill concerns electric grid interconnection rules and has no relation to healthcare policy or systems.
The bill is unrelated to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No content in the bill pertains to immigration, border policy, or related protections.
The legislation does not address reproductive rights, abortion access, or any related healthcare regulations.
No provisions involve military, defense spending, or national security appropriations.

The bill prioritizes 'dispatchable power' projects in interconnection queues to improve grid reliability. While dispatchable resources often include fossil fuels and nuclear (as opposed to intermittent renewables), the text does not directly amend environmental statutes, expand or limit environmental protections, or regulate emissions. Any link is indirect and not a genuine engagement with the topic.
The bill contains no provisions related to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net policies.
No references to schools, education funding, school choice, or federal education policy appear in the bill.
The bill does not address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance regulation.
No content relates to sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or criminal justice reform.
The legislation does not address tariffs, trade agreements, or protectionist measures.
No fiscal provisions, deficit impacts, or debt-reduction measures are included.
The bill is silent on LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil rights issues.
No provisions concern foreign assistance, international aid, or related funding.
The bill does not address voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No provisions relate to technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The bill contains no language on worker protections, union rights, or labor policy.
No content addresses religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or anti-discrimination law.
